items.label: section_header
items.text: A PROBLEM INVOLVING THE EXTRACTION OF LEAD

items.label: text
items.text: Lead is extracted from galena, PbS. The ore is roasted in air to produce lead(ll) oxide, PbO:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 P b S ( s ) + 3 O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 P b O ( s ) + 2 S O _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: The lead(ll) oxide is then converted to lead by heating it with carbon in a blast furnace:

items.label: formula
items.text: P b O ( s ) + C ( s ) \rightarrow P b ( l ) + O O ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: The molten lead is tapped from the bottom of the furnace.

items.label: text
items.text: Calculate the mass of lead that would be produced from 1 tonne of galena.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 5.17 Molten lead tapped from the bottom of a furnace.

items.label: text
items.text: We have been given the mass of PbS so we can calculate the number of moles. However, we have to be careful because the mass is in tonnes but to calculate a number of moles we need to know the mass in grams, so we must convert tonnes to grams. The conversion for this is shown in Figure 5.18. Just write down this relationship: 1 tonne is equivalent to 1 000 000 g so, to change from tonnes to grams, the number has to increase (from 1 to 1 000 000), so we multiply by 1 000000.

items.label: text
items.text: Therefore we have 1000 000g PbS.

items.label: formula
items.text: Number of m oles = \frac { \ m a s s } { \ m a s s \, o f \, 1 \, m o l e }

items.label: formula
items.text: \text {grams} \quad \text {The number of moles of PBS} = \frac { 1 0 0 0 0 0 } { 2 3 9 } = 4 1 8 4 \, m o l .

items.label: text
items.text: From the first equation:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2 P b S ( s ) + 3 O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 P b O ( s ) + 2 S O _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: we can see that 2 mol PbS produce 2 mol PbO, therefore we can work out that 4184 mol PbS will produce 4184 mol PbO.

items.label: text
items.text: From the second equation:

items.label: formula
items.text: P b O ( s ) + C ( s ) \rightarrow P b ( l ) + O O ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: we can see that 1 mol PbO produces 1 mol Pb. But we are starting this reaction with 4184 mol PbO and so we can work out that we willproduce 4184 mol Pb.

items.label: text
items.text: The mass of 4184 mol Pb is 4184 × 207 = 866000 g.
